name: Saba Mahmood
shortBio: Pakistani-born anthropologist and social theorist whose study of Cairo's women's mosque movement radically challenged secular-liberal assumptions that moral agency exists only as resistance or subversion of norms.
centralQuestion: Can ethical agency consist in the bodily cultivation and inhabitation of non-liberal religious norms rather than solely in their subversion?

keyWorks.title: Politics of Piety: The Islamic Revival and the Feminist Subject
keyWorks.description: Rethinks Aristotelian habitus and Foucauldian subjectivation through Muslim women's piety practices, reshaping contemporary social and feminist theory.

keyWorks.title: Religious Difference in a Secular Age: A Minority Report
keyWorks.description: Genealogy of modern secular governance demonstrating how the postcolonial state regulates religious difference.
